projects.title: A day on the farm, seen differently

roles.title: Observation and photography
roles.task: Observe the same place at different times, recording light, soil and changes with photos and short notes.
roles.bring: A phone and one question you are curious about.
roles.support: We are planning a way to choose observation locations and recording methods together.
roles.prepare_now: Choose a place nearby. Write three sentences about the light and colours you see right now.
roles.experience: Start with photos and notes; no experience with measuring equipment is needed.
roles.personal_output: An observation note with a location and time
roles.next_question: What might change if you return at a different time?
roles.action_label: Record the light in one place

roles.title: Working with data
roles.task: Read existing logs, find dates, units and missing values, and write down rules for cleaning the data.
roles.bring: Check the activity announcement for laptop requirements and availability.
roles.support: We are preparing source data and step-by-step examples in Korean.
roles.prepare_now: Choose what you would like to record. Write a line for the date, time, units and a symbol for values you do not know.
roles.experience: Start by reading rows and columns; coding can come later if you choose.
roles.personal_output: Your own list of fields to record
roles.next_question: How will you distinguish a missing value from zero?

roles.title: Creative interpretation
roles.task: Express the day you observed through photographs, colours or short writing, in a form that suits you.
roles.bring: Whatever you like to use for recording ideas.
roles.support: The form of expression and what to share will be agreed together.
roles.prepare_now: Think of the light on a day you remember. Express it in three colours or a short piece of writing.
roles.experience: Choose your own form; no experience with editing software is needed.
roles.personal_output: A first draft capturing light and sensory impressions
roles.next_question: What scene might someone else imagine from the same record?
roles.action_label: Capture a day in colour and words

projects.title: Tools the next person can use

roles.title: Experience using tools
roles.task: Recall a time when finding or using a tool was difficult, and write down the instructions you needed.
roles.bring: An experience you would like to improve.
roles.support: We plan to choose the actual tool together.
roles.prepare_now: Recall one recent moment when you had trouble finding or using an object. Write down what happened and what explanation would have helped.
roles.experience: Start with your own experience; no repair skills are needed.
roles.personal_output: A note describing one difficulty and the missing explanation
roles.next_question: What is the first thing a new user should know?

roles.title: Labels and instructions
roles.task: Write the name, location and conditions for use so that someone unfamiliar with the tool can understand them.
roles.bring: A pen and paper, or a phone.
roles.support: We plan to compare the content and design of labels.
roles.prepare_now: Choose an object at home. Write its name, where it belongs and any conditions for using it.
roles.experience: Start with short sentences; no experience making QR codes is needed.
roles.next_question: Are there any words a first-time reader might not understand?
roles.action_label: Explain it to a first-time user

roles.title: Repair records
roles.task: Look at a tool’s condition and record what may need repair and what needs checking.
roles.bring: Share your experience and the kinds of work you can do before starting.
roles.support: Work will be limited to tasks agreed with the person responsible.
roles.prepare_now: Describe the appearance and symptoms of an object you would like to repair. You do not need to take it apart or test it.
roles.experience: Start by recording its condition. Practical repairs come later, after experience and the person responsible have been confirmed.
roles.personal_output: A description of the condition and a list of things to check
roles.next_question: Who should you consult, and what should you check, before a repair?

roles.title: Light and form
roles.task: Use sketches and words to explore a memorable patch of light or shade from the farm.
roles.bring: A scene you would like to draw or describe.
roles.support: We plan to begin by discussing the question behind the artwork.
roles.prepare_now: Record a memorable scene of light or shade with a sketch or a few words.
roles.experience: Draw or describe it in whichever way suits you; no making experience is needed.
roles.personal_output: A sketch or description of the scene and the feeling you want to express
roles.next_question: What quality of the light would you like to capture?

roles.title: Paper structures
roles.task: Fold and layer paper to try small forms that let light through.
roles.bring: Materials will be specified in the activity announcement.
roles.support: The plan is to start with a small model.
roles.prepare_now: Draw a folded or layered paper shape. Mark where light could pass through.
roles.experience: Start with a sketch; there is no need to buy materials.
roles.personal_output: A sketch of a structure that lets light through
roles.next_question: How might a change in shape change the shadow?

roles.title: Electronics and records
roles.task: List what needs checking in the power and lighting setup, and record changes to the model.
roles.bring: Your making experience and areas of interest.
roles.support: Testing will begin only after the components and the person responsible have been confirmed.
roles.prepare_now: Write down how bright you want the light to be, where it would be used and how long it would stay on. Component connections will be considered later.
roles.experience: Start by defining requirements; circuit tests require confirmed components and a responsible person.
roles.personal_output: Lighting requirements and a list of things to check
roles.next_question: What conditions would help the light express your idea?
